title.title: A $C^1$ counterexample to the entropy conjecture
title.subtitle: Claim: a $C^1$ self-map with zero topological entropy whose homology grows like $2^n$

beats.text: Shub, 1974: growth in homology should force topological entropy
One sphere coordinate mostly squares, giving the factor 2; a circle clock can stall
Small stored signals hide the winding: $C^1$ is just enough room

achievement.label: Shub's entropy conjecture (1974), $C^1$ self-map form
statement: h_{\mathrm{top}}(f) \ge \log \rho(f_*)\ \text{ fails for some } C^1 f
achievement.context: Yomdin (1987) proved it for $C^\infty$; the counterexample lives on $S^1 \times (S^2)^{q+1}$
achievement.note: Noninvertible map: the $C^1$ diffeomorphism case remains open

verify.detail: Comparator builds the manifold concretely in Euclidean space; not in the main-results list

sources.quote: h_top(f)=0 < log 2 ≤ log ρ(f_*), disproving the general C^1 self-map form of Shub's entropy conjecture
Noninvertible map; the C^1 diffeomorphism case (the version many authors mean) remains open.
formalizes the existence statement with the manifold concretely S^1×(S^2)^{q+1} embedded in Euclidean space

plain: A map that doubles a hidden count every step, yet whose points never spread apart: growth without chaos

steps: One sphere mostly squares, doubling a count in homology
A circle clock slows almost to a stop near one reading
Extra spheres store small signals that hide the growth

voice.text: Shub predicted topological growth forces chaos. Here a sphere doubles, yet nothing spreads.
A squaring sphere, a stalling clock and small stored signals hide the growth.
Claimed: a C one counterexample, noninvertible.
